how: 20 random clusters of the 200 largest, 12 random members each (sheet2.py, seed 1 for A, seed 2 for B). For each cluster I counted the members with the same shape as the cluster's majority (outline, length, loops, tails), at native 84 px height, contrast-stretched. I do not read Mongolian; this is shape identity only. Judged once, before any LoRA read of these crops was seen.

A_pix_kmeans_K3000_all_members.notes: Short frequent forms (loop suffix, '7' form, X mark, a looped two-letter word) are clean; long words mix by length; #06 and #13 are not words (cross marks, a sliver).

B_pix_kmeans_K6000_core.notes: Core = members nearer than the cluster's 60th-percentile distance and the global 35th percentile. Clean clusters are short forms, several clusters per form: the detached loop (#00,#01,#03,#07,#10), the '7' form (#06,#14,#17), punctuation dots (#15,#19), X marks (#13,#18). One long word is clean (#11, 12/12); one long-word cluster is mixed and partly merged words (#02, 2/12).

B_long_median_width_ge40px.notes: Secondary arm (not in the brief): the same core clusters, restricted to those whose median crop is >= 40 px long, seed 3. Medium words (2-4 teeth groups, a looped initial) are clean; the longest words (> ~100 px) mix 2-4 of 12, so pixel clustering does not reach long vocabulary.
